findings.where: Screen 6 (Power in, power out), the I1/I2 current bars and the power bars
findings.what: The current and power bar scales are reset from the turns (cs = niceUp of the 2 Ω currents, ps = niceUp(V2²/2)), so in the demo itself, as N2 steps 230 to 460 turns on 10 Ω, the secondary current bar shrinks from 0.19 to 0.15 of its track while I2 doubles from 11.5 A to 23 A, and the power bars barely move (0.165 to 0.176) while the power quadruples from 1323 W to 5290 W; fix the scales per screen from the sliders' extremes, or rescale only on screen entry, so a bigger current always draws a longer bar.

The typed answer, 1.88 mWb, is printed in the question itself ("The flux peaks at 1.88 mWb"), so the figure is on screen before Check even though the flux readout shows ?; give the supply and turns instead (440 V, 60 Hz, 880 primary turns, load changed from 10 Ω to 5 Ω, secondary current doubles to 23 A: what is the peak flux now?), so he works Φm = 440 ÷ (4.44 × 60 × 880) = 1.88 mWb and the slips 3.76 and 0.94 still catch letting the load in.

The question is a 200 to 800 turn step-up on 115 V, where the primary carries the larger current, but the picture beside it shows the 880 to 230 step-down on 440 V with the I1 bar the shorter and the box at 73.2 Ω, the opposite direction; show a step-up setting (for example N1 440, N2 920, so the I1 bar is the longer) or leave the bars empty.
